tagline: A Coastal Retreat Just Steps from the Sand
welcomeMessage: Welcome to our coastal retreat, just steps from the sand in the heart of Dewey Beach. We hope you soak up the sun, salt air, and everything this little beach town has to offer. If there's ever anything we can do to make your stay better, just reach out.

checkIn.arrivalMessage: We'll send you detailed check-in instructions by message a day or two before your arrival.
checkIn.parkingNote: There's a private driveway with space for three cars, so no one has to circle for street parking after arriving.
checkIn.doorLockNote: The door code is 3332. Please remember to lock up whenever you're off the property.

checkOut.notice: You'll receive detailed check-out instructions by message 18 hours before your check-out time.
checkOut.trash: Please take out any trash and recycling and place it in the appropriate bins. There's a valet service, so no need to place the bins anywhere else.
checkOut.windows: Please close any windows and lock all doors when you leave.
checkOut.thermostat: Please leave the Nest thermostat at COOL 72° in the summer and HEAT 65° in the winter — please don't turn it off.

houseRules: Renters must be 25 years of age or older
Please don't tape or glue anything to the walls without prior approval
Please don't park in the front yard — there's room for three cars in the driveway

localRecommendations.name: Dewey Beach
localRecommendations.note: The wide, easygoing home beach — quieter than Rehoboth, dog-friendly outside summer hours.

localRecommendations.name: Poodle Beach
localRecommendations.note: The southern end of Rehoboth's beach, known for a laid-back, welcoming crowd.

localRecommendations.name: Rehoboth Beach
localRecommendations.note: Wide sandy beach right alongside the boardwalk, shops, and Funland.

localRecommendations.name: Towers Beach
localRecommendations.note: A quieter, less crowded stretch near Cape Henlopen — good for an escape from the boardwalk scene.

localRecommendations.name: Deauville Beach
localRecommendations.note: Free parking, dog-friendly off-season, and usually much less crowded.

localRecommendations.name: BAKED Coffee Bar
localRecommendations.note: Tiny coffee bar with excellent pastries — the cinnamon roll is locally famous.

localRecommendations.name: The Coffee Mill
localRecommendations.note: Easygoing Dewey Beach coffee shop with a self-serve cream and sugar bar.

localRecommendations.name: The Dewey Post
localRecommendations.note: Beloved breakfast spot — the waffles and chicken & waffles are the draw.

localRecommendations.name: Fish Hawk's Restaurant
localRecommendations.note: A newer, more upscale coastal spot — craft cocktails and elevated small plates.

localRecommendations.name: Starboard Raw
localRecommendations.note: Baltimore-style oyster bar from the Starboard team — fresh raw bar and cold beer.

localRecommendations.name: Woody's Dewey Beach
localRecommendations.note: A Dewey institution — locals will tell you it has the best crab cakes at the beach.

localRecommendations.name: La Fable
localRecommendations.note: Intimate French bistro on Baltimore Ave — escargot, steak frites, and a piano bar on Saturdays.

localRecommendations.name: The Local Bootlegging Co.
localRecommendations.note: Prohibition-themed speakeasy with elevated comfort food and inventive cocktails.

localRecommendations.name: Lewes Oyster House
localRecommendations.note: Historic oyster house in downtown Lewes — raw bar, rotisserie chicken, great burgers.

localRecommendations.name: Heirloom
localRecommendations.note: Farm-to-table fine dining in a converted Lewes house — seasonal, imaginative, a local favorite.

localRecommendations.name: Kindle
localRecommendations.note: Seasonal American fare with French touches — candlelit dining room in downtown Lewes.

localRecommendations.name: Somewhere
localRecommendations.note: Tropical Caribbean-coastal brunch spot with a sand-filled outdoor Oasis patio.

localRecommendations.name: Drift Seafood & Raw Bar
localRecommendations.note: Small, elevated seafood spot on Baltimore Ave — fresh oysters and a tight, seasonal menu.

localRecommendations.name: Dewey Beer Co.
localRecommendations.note: Local brewpub with hop-forward ales and fruited sours — a Dewey favorite.

localRecommendations.name: The Starboard
localRecommendations.note: The Dewey Beach institution — Bloody Mary bar, live music, and a 60-year history.

localRecommendations.name: Northbeach
localRecommendations.note: Bayfront live music and dance venue with sunset views and a Friday pizza party.

localRecommendations.name: Rusty Rudder
localRecommendations.note: Bayfront deck with live music daily — a classic Dewey Beach sunset spot.

localRecommendations.name: Bottle & Cork
localRecommendations.note: Legendary concert venue — a Dewey Beach tradition for touring national acts.

localRecommendations.name: Dewey Beach Parasail
localRecommendations.note: Soar above the bay for sweeping views of Dewey and the coastline.

localRecommendations.name: Rehoboth Beach Boardwalk
localRecommendations.note: A mile of classic boardwalk charm — arcades, shops, and ice cream.

localRecommendations.name: Funland
localRecommendations.note: Nostalgic family amusement park right on the boardwalk — a Rehoboth tradition since 1962.

localRecommendations.name: Cape Henlopen State Park
localRecommendations.note: Bike and hiking trails, a WWII fire control tower, and a huge stretch of protected beach.

localRecommendations.name: John Waples Memorial Playground
localRecommendations.note: A shaded, fenced-in playground — a nice break from the beach for kids.

faq.question: Are linens and towels included?
faq.answer: Yes — all sheets and towels are cleaned and turned over after every stay.

faq.question: Do we have beach chairs and beach toys?
faq.answer: We don't currently have a shed or outdoor storage for beach gear, so we ask that you bring your own. Chairs and umbrellas are also available to rent right on the beach.

faq.question: Can I access the roof deck?
faq.answer: Yes, you're welcome to! Just please use it at your own risk — the stairs and access can be steep, and the wood up there is somewhat dated and beginning to warp in areas. Enjoy the view, but take care.

faq.question: How do the TVs work?
faq.answer: The smart TVs run Roku, so they're simple to navigate — just use the purple remote to browse and launch your streaming apps. If you get stuck, here's the official Roku TV user guide.

faq.question: Do I need to take the trash/recycling to the end of the driveway?
faq.answer: No — there's a valet service that takes care of this. Your only job is to make sure you put the trash and recycling in the right bin!
